title: 1921 student garden planting and harvesting as a school subject
description: In the spring of 1921, the school garden on the grounds of Hartland Superior School, also known as McMullin Flat, was assigned to students, who were given seeds and the use of the school’s tools to cultivate, plant, and harvest their own plots. On September 26, 1921, the first school fair was held at Sipprelle’s Garage (across from the school garden plots). Other schools, such as Somerville, Waterville, Coldstream, and Brighten, joined Hartland to exhibit the results of their school gardens, home gardens, pig and poultry clubs, home efficiency projects, and domestic science departments. Judges in each department awarded prizes to those who excelled in their school exhibits.
